latin: Rēgulus. — Istō modo tū quoque dē caelō venīs? In quā stēllā errantī nātus es<sup>1</sup>?
Antōnius. — Ergō tū, dē stēllā aliā venīs?
Ille autem nōn respondit: nam leviter renuēns<sup>2</sup> māchinam meam intuēbātur<sup>3</sup>.
Reg. — Enimvērō ista māchinā ē locīs nōn valdē longinquīs advehī potuistī*...
Rēgulus ex Antōniō multa percontātus est quae, propter locī inopiam, omittere dēbuimus. Dē peregrīnātiōnibus ejus astronautīcīs aliquantula excerpere māluimus*.

... Cum ille ad stellulās 325, 326, 327, 328, 329, 330 (prononcez trecentēsimam vīcēsimam quīntam, etc... trecentēsimam trīcēsimam) propius accessisset, eās vīsere īnstituit ut et occupātiōnem quaereret et doctrīnā sē exōrnāre posset<sup>4</sup>.
Prīmam rēx incolēbat. Sedēbat rēx purpurā pellibusque mūris ponticī<sup>5</sup> indūtus, in soliō<sup>6</sup> simplicissimē factō, sed tamen magnificō.
Rēx. — Attat! Ecce parēns quī mihi pāret<sup>7</sup>.
Rēgulus. — Quōmodo mē agnōscere<sup>8</sup> potest*, quoniam<sup>9</sup> mē nunquam vīdit?
Rēx. — Accēde propius ut tē melius adspiciam...
Reg. — Ō, Rēx, quae imperiō<sup>10</sup> rēgis?
Rēx, simplicissimē. — Ūniversa.
Reg. — Stēllaene tibi pārent?
Rēx. — Sānē quidem, et statim pārent; neglegī jussa mea<sup>11</sup> nōn patior.
latinAccented: Rḗgulus. — Istō modo tū quoque dē caelō venīs? In quā stēllā errántī nātus es<sup>1</sup>?
Antṓnius. — Ergō tū, dē stēllā áliā venīs?
Ille autem nōn respóndit: nam léviter rénuēns<sup>2</sup> mā́chinam meam intuēbā́tur<sup>3</sup>.
Reg. — Enimvḗrō ista mā́chinā ē locīs nōn valdē longínquīs ádvehī potuístī*...
Rḗgulus ex Antṓniō multa percontā́tus est quae, propter locī inópiam, omíttere dēbúimus. Dē peregrīnātiṓnibus ejus astronautī́cīs aliquántula excérpere mālúimus*.

... Cum ille ad stéllulās 325, 326, 327, 328, 329, 330 (pronóncez trecentḗsimam vīcḗsimam quīntam, etc... trecentḗsimam trīcḗsimam) própius accessísset, eās vī́sere īnstítuit ut et occupātiṓnem quáereret et doctrī́nā sē exōrnā́re posset<sup>4</sup>.
Prīmam rēx incolḗbat. Sedḗbat rēx púrpurā pellibúsque mūris pónticī<sup>5</sup> indū́tus, in sóliō<sup>6</sup> simplicíssimē factō, sed tamen magníficō.
Rēx. — Attat! Ecce parēns quī mihi pāret<sup>7</sup>.
Rḗgulus. — Quṓmodo mē agnṓscere<sup>8</sup> potest*, quóniam<sup>9</sup> mē nunquam vīdit?
Rēx. — Accḗde própius ut tē mélius adspíciam...
Reg. — Ō, Rēx, quae impériō<sup>10</sup> rēgis?
Rēx, simplicíssimē. — Ūnivérsa.
Reg. — Stēlláene tibi pārent?
Rēx. — Sānē quidem, et statim pārent; néglegī jussa mea<sup>11</sup> nōn pátior.
english: The little prince. — [So] (in this way), you too come from the sky? [On] which [planet] (wandering star) were you born?
Antoine. — So you, you come from another star?
But he did not answer: shaking his head gently, he was looking at my machine.
Prince. — It's true that with this machine you couldn't have [come from very far] (from very distant places to be transported)...
The little prince asked Antoine many things which, by reason of the lack of space, we have had to omit. We have preferred to extract a few little things from his astronautical journeys.

... As he happened nearer to the [little stars] [asteroids] 325, 326, 327, 328, 329, 330, he undertook to visit them in order to look for an occupation there and to [instruct himself] (that he might adorn himself with teaching).
A king lived on the first. The king sat, dressed in purple and [ermine] (in skins of rat of Pontus) on a throne made very simply, but nevertheless majestic.
The king. — Well, well! There's a subject who is going to obey me (subj.).
The prince. — How can he recognize me, since he has never seen me?
The king. — Come closer, so that I may see you better...
The prince. — O, King, [over what] (by what) [do you reign] (govern by) [your] empire?
The king, in all simplicity. — Everything.
The prince. — Do the stars obey you?
The king. — Certainly, and they obey immediately; I do not [tolerate] [that] my orders [be neglected].

footnotes: Nascor, -eris, nasci, natus sum, to be born; here in the perfect (pres. of the perfectum) since it is a past action whose effect continues in the present (if A. had not been born, R. could not have spoken to him!). Stella errans or planeta: this last word, of Greek origin, precisely means wandering star.
Renuo, -is, -ere, -ui, v.i., to make a negative sign with the head.
Intueor, -eris, -eri, -itus sum, to look at attentively (dep. v. t.).

In phrase 6, note that the main clause is in the perfect (instituit), that the subordinate introduced by cum is in the pluperfect of the subjunctive, but that those introduced by ut are in the imperfect subjunctive (quaereret, posset).
Ponticus, -a, -um, of Pontus, region of Asia Minor. Pellis, -is, f., the skin of an animal, the fur; cutis, -is, f., the skin of man.

Pareo, -es, -ere, -ui, -itum + dat., to obey. Do not confuse its present participle, parens, -entis, obeying, here taken as a noun and meaning subject, with parens (a short), the parent (father or mother).
Imperium, -ii, n., power; from imperare, to command.

Jussa, n. pl., comes from jubeo, -es, -ere, jussi, jussum, to order; this verb is construed with the infinitive clause (e.g.: jubeo te exire, I order you to go out), whereas impero is construed with ut + subj.
comments: From the work cited (opere citato) by Bourgeois and Lupin, Exercices latins, p. 15 (Hachette, Paris).

Sino, -is, -ere, sivi, situm + inf. or subj., to permit. Do not confuse the imperative of this verb with the preposition sine (+ abl.): sine fine, without end. — Aedilis, -is, m., aedile, municipal councillor (from aedes). — Moneo, -es, -ere, -ui, -itum, to warn. — Vincio, -is, -ire, vinxi, vinctum, to tie; not to be confused with vinco, -is, -ere, vici, victum, to conquer. To which conjugation do these two verbs belong? — The first belongs to the 4th (inf. in ire, second-last syllable long), the second to the 3rd (inf. in ere, with short e). — Neuter = ne uter, neither the one nor the other. Such is the case of the neuter gender (neutrum), which is neither masculine nor feminine. — Culter, -tri, m., the knife. — Rubigo, -inis, f., rust. — Volumen, -inis, n., roll, book, volume; comes from volvere, to roll. Formerly the paper of books was rolled on itself, and not superposed in successive pages. One could therefore wrap different things in the paper of an old book. Do you remember volumen tabaceum (L. 38, N. 1)? — Repeto, -is, -ere, ivi or ii, itum, to ask back. Do you remember petere, to make for, to go and fetch or to ask for something? (e.g. petere rem ab aliquo).

latin: Quis hunc libellum prōposuit?
Prīmum sine eum legam!
Aedīlēs monent: heri post mercātum in forō boāriō inventa sunt;
ānulus vidēlicet aureus; pileus lāneus; crepida trītissima;
ēbrius quīdam oblītus nōminis suī;
asinus vīnctus ad columnam (fortasse ēbriī, sed neuter loquitur);
culter rūbīginōsus; pūpa lignea;
volūmen philosophicum plēnum intibōrum;
canis flāvus sine caudā;
infāns nūdus in acervō foliōrum brassicārum.
Haec omnia repetenda sunt ā scrībīs rērum inventārum.
Respondet ad quaestiōnem tuam ultima sententia: scrība quīdam libellum prōposuit.
latinAccented: Quis hunc libéllum prōpósuit?
Prīmum sine eum legam!
Aedī́lēs monent: heri post mercā́tum in forō boā́riō invénta sunt;
ā́nulus vidḗlicet áureus; píleus lā́neus; crépida trītíssima;
ḗbrius quīdam oblī́tus nṓminis suī;
ásinus vīnctus ad colúmnam (fortásse ḗbriī, sed néuter lóquitur);
culter rūbīginṓsus; pūpa lígnea;
volū́men philosóphicum plēnum intibṓrum;
canis flāvus sine caudā;
infāns nūdus in acérvō foliṓrum brassicā́rum.
Haec ómnia repeténda sunt ā scrībīs rērum inventā́rum.
Respóndet ad quaestiṓnem tuam última senténtia: scrība quīdam libéllum prōpósuit.
english: Who put up this notice?
First [let me] read it!
[The town council announces] (the aediles warn): yesterday, after the market, in the cattle market, (the following objects) were found:
namely: a gold ring; a woollen cap; a very worn sandal;
a drunkard who has forgotten his name;
a donkey tied to a column (perhaps [that] of the drunkard, but neither the one nor the other speaks);
a rusty knife; a wooden doll;
a philosophical book full of endives;
a yellow dog without a tail;
a naked baby in a pile of cabbage leaves.
All this is to be claimed from the lost property clerks.
[Your question is answered by] the last sentence: it was an employee who put up the notice.
